title: Finite purity as a normalized system of explicit adjunctions
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $\mathcal C_T(\Lambda)=\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ for the bounded constructible finite-Tor pro-etale condensed-module category [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $F_{f,\Lambda}=Rf_{!,\Lambda}$, $G_{f,\Lambda}=f^!_\Lambda$ with its specified restricted adjunction $F_{f,\Lambda}\dashv G_{f,\Lambda}$ and counit $\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda}$ [sk-thm-existence], and $J_{f,\Lambda}=f^*_\Lambda(-)(d)[2d]$ with the Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

Let $A$ range over finite commutative rings killed by a power of $\ell$, with finite-$A$ twists, inverse diagonal/DNC orientation and tensor-transpose maps $\gamma^A:J_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f,A}$ specified in [det-sp-finite-general-ring]. Finite module categories are compared with the condensed categories by the exact section-action derived equivalence of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. For $A\to B$, use derived scalar extension $T^T_{A,B}$, the compact-support comparison $b_{A,B}:T^Y_{A,B}F_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f,B}T^X_{A,B}$ and the exceptional comparison $c_{A,B}:T^X_{A,B}G_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f,B}T^Y_{A,B}$ of [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities], and the canonical source comparison $a_{A,B}:T^X_{A,B}J_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{f,B}T^Y_{A,B}$.

The maps $t^A_K=\varepsilon_{f,A,K}\circ F_{f,A}(\gamma^A_K)$ are counits of adjunctions $F_{f,A}\dashv J_{f,A}$ on these same categories, independent of the exponent chosen to annihilate $A$. Under the specified comparisons,
$$t^B_{K_B}\circ F_{f,B}(a_{A,B,K})=T^Y_{A,B}(t^A_K)\circ b_{A,B,J_{f,A}K}^{-1}.$$
The induced source coefficient comparisons and these adjunctions are transitive for $A\to B\to C$. Their purity maps satisfy $c_{A,B,K}\circ T^X_{A,B}(\gamma^A_K)=\gamma^B_{K_B}\circ a_{A,B,K}$, the orientation/tensor composition and Cartesian base-change identities of [det-sp-composition-factors, det-sp-purity-bc-factors], and all finite-reduction trace identities of [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]. In particular this is a system of adjunctions and specified counits, not just a family of objectwise isomorphisms.

For an affine-line projection $p:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$, the counit is $(1_K\otimes I_S)\circ\mathrm{PF}^{-1}$, where $I_S$ is projective-line integration restricted by extension by zero and the diagonal orientation is the integration-transposed normalization of [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement]. Iteration gives the corresponding affine-space normalization, also for arbitrary nonregular finite $A$.

proof.text: Use the exact section-action equivalence of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation, lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence] to identify ordinary finite-module and condensed-module categories, tensor products and the same compactification composite $F_A$. The specified restricted adjunction remains $F_A\dashv G_A$, with its counit. By [det-sp-finite-general-ring](3), $\gamma^A:J_A\to G_A$ is a natural isomorphism independent of the annihilating exponent. If $\Phi_A$ denotes the specified adjunction bijection, set $\Psi_A(u)=(\gamma^A_K)^{-1}\Phi_A(u)$ for $u:F_AM\to K$. This is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(F_AM,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,J_AK)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] its unit is $(\gamma^A_{F_AM})^{-1}\eta^A_M$ and its counit is $\varepsilon^A_KF_A(\gamma^A_K)=t^A_K$. This proves the triangle identities and exponent independence on the stated categories, without identifying $\Dctf$ with all bounded constructible complexes over a nonregular ring.

source.place: Step 1, finite purity; Step 3, same left functor and restricted adjunction

proof.text:
For $A\to B$, [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](2) ensures all scalar-extended inputs are still in $\Dctf$, without flatness. Write $T_X,T_Y$ for extension. Clause (3) of [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities] says precisely $c_KT_X(\gamma^A_K)=\gamma^B_{K_B}a_K$. The defining counit equation of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] and naturality of $b$ in [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], evaluated at $\gamma^A_K:J_AK\to G_AK$, give
$$\begin{aligned}t^B_{K_B}F_B(a_K)&=\varepsilon^B_{K_B}F_B(c_K)F_BT_X(\gamma^A_K)\\&=T_Y(\varepsilon^A_K)b_{G_AK}^{-1}F_BT_X(\gamma^A_K)\\&=T_Y(\varepsilon^A_K)T_YF_A(\gamma^A_K)b_{J_AK}^{-1}=T_Y(t^A_K)b_{J_AK}^{-1}.\end{aligned}$$
Both sides start at $F_BT_XJ_AK$ and end at $T_YK$. Thus this is the required equation of actual counits, not merely an isomorphism of their source objects.

source.place: Step 1, coefficient compatibility of the exceptional adjunction

proof.text:
The preceding purity equation expresses the specified source comparison as $a_{A,B}=\gamma_B^{-1}c_{A,B}T_X\gamma_A$. For $A\to B\to C$, substitute this expression into the two successive source comparisons. The adjacent factors $T_{B,C}(\gamma_B)T_{B,C}(\gamma_B^{-1})$ cancel. Clause (2) of [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities] then identifies the remaining exceptional comparison with $c_{A,C}$, and naturality of the scalar associator in [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](4) identifies the remaining $\gamma_A$ factor with its direct extension. Explicitly, with those associators denoted by $\alpha^X,\alpha^Y$,
$$J_C(\alpha^Y_K)a_{B,C,K_B}T^X_{B,C}(a_{A,B,K})=a_{A,C,K}\alpha^X_{J_AK}.$$
The $b$ cocycle is exactly the last equation of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. The unit equation also transfers: substitute $\eta^{J,A}=\gamma_A^{-1}\eta^A$ and $a=\gamma_B^{-1}cT_X\gamma_A$ into $J_B(b_M)a_{F_AM}T_X(\eta^{J,A}_M)$; naturality of $\gamma_B$ and [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](1) reduce this to $\gamma_{B,F_BM_B}^{-1}\eta^B_{M_B}=\eta^{J,B}_{M_B}$. Together with Step 2, this proves transitivity as adjunctions with specified units and counits.

Apply the finite-ring alternatives of [det-sp-composition-factors] and [det-sp-purity-bc-factors] to these same $\gamma^A$. Their statements use exactly the inverse diagonal orientation and the counit-transpose tensor map of [det-sp-finite-general-ring], so they give both the constituent identities and the asserted purity composition and Cartesian exchange equations. No tower case is needed. At $A=A_{E,n}$ and $B=A_{E,m}$, $1\leq m\leq n$, [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] supplies the reduction squares for orientations, traces, composition and base change. The coefficient-valued smooth trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace] is exactly $\varepsilon^A_KF_A(\gamma^A_K)$, hence the $t^A_K$ just constructed; there is no additional trace to identify. These results apply with the original smoothness, pure-dimension and separated finite-type hypotheses.

source.place: Step 1, orientations, smooth traces, composition and Cartesian squares

proof.text:
For any finite $A$, put $L=A_X(d)[2d]$, $\omega=G_AA_Y$, and write $v:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega$ for the inverse orientation. By the specification in [det-sp-finite-general-ring], $\gamma_K=\theta_K(1\otimes v)$, where $\theta_K$ is the transpose of inverse coefficient-first projection followed by $1_K\otimes\varepsilon^A_{A_Y}$. The transpose formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] therefore gives, by naturality of that projection in $v$,
$$t^A_K=(1_K\otimes\varepsilon^A_{A_Y})\mathrm{PF}_{\omega,K}^{-1}F_A(1\otimes v)=(1_K\otimes[\varepsilon^A_{A_Y}F_A(v)])\mathrm{PF}_{L,K}^{-1}.$$
The bracket is $t^A_{A_Y}$, since the unit component of the twist reassociation identifies $\gamma_{A_Y}$ with $v$. Unit constraints are understood. Consequently knowing the trace at the coefficient unit determines this counit for every $K$; $K$ need not be a scalar extension of a complex over a smaller ring.

source.place: Step 4, integration normalization; tensor-transpose construction underlying Step 1

proof.text: First take $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$, equivalently $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ at level $n$. For $p:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$, [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] identifies the specified diagonal/DNC $\gamma_{p,K}$ with the exceptional transpose of $(1_K\otimes I_{R,S})\mathrm{PF}^{-1}$. Applying the inverse adjunction bijection, as stated in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], gives $t^R_K=(1_K\otimes I_{R,S})\mathrm{PF}^{-1}$ and in particular $t^R_{R_S}=I_{R,S}$. The agreement lemma explicitly fixes the inverse integration-transposed normal-bundle arrow; hence this uses the required orientation, including its scalar normalization.

Now let $A$ be any finite ring with $\ell^nA=0$, and apply Step 2 to $R\to A$ at $K=R_S$. The coefficient-unit and Tate identifications give
$$t^A_{A_S}F_{p,A}(a_{R,A,R_S})b_{R,A,J_RR_S}=T^S_{R,A}(I_{R,S}).$$
The actual projective traces, their open restrictions and their ordered affine traces satisfy this same scalar equation by [lem-pur-vector-trace-scalar-descent], with $N=\ell^n$. Its ordinary-etale coefficient maps are the proper-counit/open-tensor maps. The site/coefficient square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] carries this identity to exactly the $b$ just displayed, and the tensor/projection and counit comparisons of [lem-pur-finite-ring-site-tensor-transpose] give the same pro-etale trace. Since $F(a)b$ is invertible, $t^A_{A_S}=I_{A,S}$. All schemes used are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the Noetherian field spectrum. Step 5 now gives $t^A_K=(1_K\otimes I_{A,S})\mathrm{PF}^{-1}$ for every $K$. This uses scalar extension only for the coefficient unit, and imposes neither regularity on $A$ nor flatness over $R$.

source.place: Step 4, finite affine integration normalization extended to arbitrary finite rings

proof.text: Finally factor $p_d:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ into its ordered $d$ line projections. The composition formula already cited in Step 4 identifies $\gamma_{p_d}$ with their iterated purity maps, under the specified source reassociations. Compose their Hom bijections from Step 1. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], the resulting counit for two stages is $t_{g,K}\circ F_g(t_{f,J_gK})$, preceded by the inverse compact-support compositor. Substitution of the composition formula for $\gamma$ into $\varepsilon_{gf}F_{gf}(\gamma_{gf})$ gives that same expression, since the exceptional compositor in [det-sp-composition-factors] is adjunction-preserving. Induction on $d$, starting with the identity adjunction at $d=0$, proves the iterated affine-space normalization. Step 7 supplies each line factor over the arbitrary finite ring $A$. Even shifts $[2d]$ introduce no extra odd-degree interchange, and the ordered construction needs no change of coordinate order.
